questions.question: Explain why stainless steel is used for surgical instruments whereas mild steel is not, despite both being ferrous metals.

points.text: Stainless steel has 10.5%+ chromium which forms a passive chromium oxide layer - self-healing, prevents rust even when scratched. Mild steel has no chromium and rusts rapidly.

questions.question: Justify the use of aluminium rather than steel for aircraft fuselage construction.

points.text: Aluminium: density 2.7 g/cm3 vs steel 7.8 - 1/3 the weight, crucial for fuel efficiency; corrosion-resistant; good strength-to-weight when alloyed. Trade-off: more expensive and less stiff.

questions.question: A product designer needs a gold-coloured, corrosion-resistant material for a door handle. Compare brass and gold-anodised aluminium.

points.text: Brass: genuine gold appearance, naturally corrosion-resistant, heavy and tactile (premium feel), low friction, antimicrobial. Gold-anodised aluminium: lighter, cheaper, coating can scratch to reveal silver beneath. For a door handle: brass is superior.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response A company is designing a lightweight camping stove. Compare aluminium and mild steel for the main body, justifying your recommendation with reference to at least four properties. <div class="

points.text: A grade 9 response will: compare Density (aluminium 2.7 vs steel 7.8 g/cm3), Thermal conductivity (205 vs 50 W/mK), Corrosion (aluminium oxide layer vs steel rusts), Strength (steel stronger but aluminium thicker walls can match strength while remaining lighter). Conclusion: aluminium for the main body.
